subject: Action items: request/response log handling and PII controls for AcmeHealth
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Lara Quinn <lara.quinn@acmehealth.com>, AcmeHealth Security <security@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-07T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Action items: request/response log handling and PII controls for AcmeHealth

Hi Lara / Acme team,

Thanks for the productive call today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned. High-level points we covered: 

- Logging surface: request headers, response payloads, and per-request metadata (trace IDs, route, latency).
- PII exposure: a few headers ("X-User-Email", "X-Session-Id") and JSON fields in request bodies may contain PHI/PII depending on your integration.
- Residency/retention needs: you mentioned US-only residency and a 24-month retention baseline for audit data.
- Redaction options discussed: header masking (regex), trace-id pseudonymization (prefix-preserving hashing), request-body tokenization or drop-before-store, and field-level allowlists/denylists.

Immediate asks / next steps (proposed):
1) Acme: share a small sample (sanitized) request/response pair and a simple data map (which fields you consider PHI/PII). We need this to recommend an exact scrubbing config.
2) Redwood: send a short tech note with the redaction patterns we recommend + retention TTL options and where data is stored. (I attached a one-pager: redwood-log-redaction-options.pdf)
3) Schedule a 60-min security deep-dive to walk through our implementation and the PoC scope. Suggested window: week of Sep 15.
4) Marissa to coordinate commercial/POC scope and any hoops re: NDA / SOW.

Questions I still have: do you have a hard requirement to never persist full request bodies (i.e., only keep hashed tokens)? Also, is there a specific schema for trace IDs you need preserved for correlating across systems?

I'll follow up with the tech note and a proposed PoC SOW draft.

Thanks,

Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-log-redaction-options.pdf (1 page summary)

From: Lara Quinn <lara.quinn@acmehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: AcmeHealth Security <security@acmehealth.com>, Tom Benson <tbenson@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2025-09-07T17:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Action items: request/response log handling and PII controls for AcmeHealth

Jonas — thanks for the summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Residency: must be US only (us-east) for the PoC and production.
- Retention: 24 months for audit logs, but access-restricted. Transactional request bodies containing PHI must be deletable on-demand.
- Trace IDs: we use a 128-bit UUID in the format aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee. We need to retain the ability to correlate across systems but cannot keep the raw UUID in plain text in persistent logs.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: 
1) pseudonymize trace IDs such that the same external UUID maps to the same pseudonym across lookups but cannot be reversed without a key;
2) provide an API to purge all persisted request bodies for a customer (or set TTLs per dataset)?

We'll prepare a small sample sanitized request/response and a data map (will share by EOD Sep 9). Also looping in our security team for the deep-dive.

--
Lara Quinn
Director, Platform Security
AcmeHealth
lara.quinn@acmehealth.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-08T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Action items: request/response log handling and PII controls for AcmeHealth

Jonas / Marissa — quick technical note to use in the security deep-dive and the tech note attachment: 

- Trace-ID handling: we support HMAC-based pseudonymization with a customer-key option (HMAC-SHA256, truncated to 128 bits) so the same input => same pseudonym but is non-reversible without the key. We can also support prefix-preserving transformations if you need partial ordering preserved (tradeoff: weaker anonymity).
- Headers/body redaction: configurable regex masks for headers; field-level scrubbing for JSON request bodies using a path-based allowlist/denylist. We can run scrubbing inline (request pipeline) so the raw body never persists, or we can store an encrypted blob with access controls.
- Retention / purge: per-customer TTLs are available on Dedicated and Private. Hosted API supports configurable retention buckets and an on-demand purge API (we'll log the purge/deletion event in audit logs).
- Residency: for US-only residency, recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private deployment; hosted accounts can be pinned to us-east region depending on capacity and contract.

Deliverables for the PoC we should propose:
- PoC test harness: 5000 synthetic requests/day for 1 week to validate redaction and correlation.
- Sandbox deployment: us-east pinned, retention TTL set to 730 days for audit buckets, bodies dropped-before-persist for transactional streams.
- Endpoint: a small example config (we can draft) + sample scrubbing rules.

I'll draft the tech note and example config by tomorrow. Assigning: Jonas to send sample from Acme when received; Marissa to prepare SOW/NDA drafts.

-Aditya
Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
